full_judgment: 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that the petitioners herein as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.103 of 1998 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna against the respondent herein impleading the Government as defendant No.2, for specific performance of contract. The plaintiffs contended, inter alia, that some lands of SA khatian Nos.223, 224, 225, 226, 227, 228, 229, 911 and 914 of Mouza-Karaitala and Maitha belonged to the predecessor of the plaintiffs, MA Zaman alias Md Hatem Ali and three others in equal share. MA Zaman resided with his family by making dwelling huts in some portion of his share. Among the above lands some lands were acquisitioned and requisitioned through different LA cases and 0.77 acre land was in Khas possession of MA Zaman and three others. MA Zaman used to possess his 4 annas share covering 0.19112 acre land. Defendant No.1 is a son of his consanguine sister Amena Khatun, who along with MA Zaman, Amzad Ali and Younus Miah, acquired the above mentioned lands by a registered deed dated 26-9-1960 with necessary permission of the Government and used to possess the same. Thereafter, MA Zaman getting his share mutated his name in a separate jama and used to possess the same by paying rents and by opening a separate municipal holding. MA Zaman in his old age appointed defendant No. 1 as his Attorney by a registered power of attorney to derequisition the land which was declared as unused land by the Government and for this purpose defendant No.1 obtained signature of MA Zaman on cartridge paper on the plea of filing a petition to bring the Sub-Registrar to his house. His son Zakir Hossain and son-in-law Altaf Hossain also put their respective signature in those papers in good faith. As required by MA Zaman, defendant No.1 on 10-3-1990 in presence of the witness refused to inform him of the existence of any case, rather they then disclosed that MA Zaman executed and registered a heba-hil-ewaj deed in his favour with respect to the suit land. Thereafter, MA Zaman filed Title Suit No.84 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge. Barguna for setting aside that heba-bil-ewaj deed since the said deed was forged and fraudulent one. Both defendant Nos.1 and 2 also filed written statements in that suit. During pendency of the suit MA Zaman died on 3-9-1993 at his residence and the plaintiffs got themselves substituted in that suit as his legal heirs. In the written statement defendant No.1 mentioned some imaginary and concocted stories terming MA Zaman as a benamder of his mother Amena with respect to the suit land and also asserting that MA Zaman refused to return that benami land in favour of defendant No.1 and his brothers and sisters and on receipt of Taka 60,000 from them executed an unregistered bainapatra deed on 3rd Magh. 1395 BS to the effect that within 10-9-1993 he would execute and register a sale deed in their favour with respect to the lands. But in spite of executing a kabala deed MA Zaman mentioning a nominal consideration money executed and registered a heba-bil-ewaj instead thereof in favour of defendant No.1 in respect of the said lands and handed over possession. In the written statement defendant No.2 simply stated that the Government has been in possession of the lands acquired by it. To avoid litigation the plaintiffs agreed to that false and unreasonable proposal of defendant No.1 and decided not to proceed with Title Suit No.84 of 1992 and, as such, the same was dismissed for default on 5-10-1993: Thereafter, on 10-9-1993 plaintiff Nos.l-3 along with Altaf Hossain son-in-law of MA Zaman in presence of District Freedom Fighter Commander Shajahan Miah and many other influential persons paid an amount of Taka 60,000 to defendant No.1 as per demand on condition that as soon as possible defendant No.I would execute and register a kabala deed in their favour in respect of the suit land when the plaintiff asked for the same. But defendant No.1 did not do so on some plea or other and further undertook to do the same as per his convenience. But on 24-9-1998 defendant No.1 refused to execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land and, hence they filed the suit.
